topic: CrowdStrike global IT outage on July 19, 2024

fact_checks.description: The outage is anchored to July 19, 2024
matching_facts: On July 19, 2024, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike pushed an update to its software that caused some devices running the Windows operating system to crash.

fact_checks.description: CrowdStrike Falcon is identified as the affected product
matching_facts: the American cybersecurity company CrowdStrike distributed a faulty update to its Falcon Sensor security software

fact_checks.description: Windows systems are identified as affected
matching_facts: Computers running macOS and Linux were unaffected, as the problematic content file was only for Windows
The impact to companies in the Central United States was exacerbated by an unrelated outage with Microsoft Azure the previous day.
The issue impacted Microsoft Windows machines running Falcon sensor for Windows version 7.11.
On July 19, 2024, cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike pushed an update to its software that caused some devices running the Windows operating system to crash.

Update 9:45 a.m., EDT, July 21, 2024:
Microsoft released a recovery tool that uses a USB drive to boot and repair affected systems.

fact_checks.description: A faulty content/software update is identified as the trigger
matching_facts: On July 19, 2024, a global IT outage was triggered by a faulty update from CrowdStrike, a leading cybersecurity firm.
The culprit? A faulty automatic sensor configuration update.
